title: JMAP as operator configuration interface
description:
Expose server configuration and status through JMAP custom capabilities and object mappings, so an operator with a standard JMAP client (Thunderbird, Fastmail, custom CLI) never needs a separate admin dashboard for day-to-day operations.

Why this issue exists:
The admin HTTP endpoint (port 9090) is sufficient for scripting but requires a separate tool. JMAP is already the user-facing interface and is HTTP/JSON. Surfacing config state as JMAP objects means the operator's email client becomes a zero-UI configuration dashboard.

Two layers of this feature:

## Layer 1: Group subscription via Mailbox/set (high value, low complexity)

Map newsgroup subscription to JMAP Mailbox lifecycle:
- Creating a Mailbox whose name matches a newsgroup pattern causes the server to subscribe to that group (add to [groups] names)
- Destroying a Mailbox unsubscribes from the group
- Mailbox properties expose article count, log tip CID, last activity timestamp
- This requires no custom capability — it reuses the standard JMAP Mailbox object
- Result: operator subscribes to comp.lang.rust by creating a folder in Thunderbird

## Layer 2: Custom capability for operator status (read-only dashboard)

Define capability urn:ietf:params:jmap:usenet-ipfs-admin and expose:
- Peer/get — list connected peers, their addresses, last-seen, article counts
- GroupLog/get — per-group log tip CID, entry count, last reconcile timestamp
- ServerStatus/get — uptime, article count, block store usage, signing key fingerprint
- These are read-only get methods; no set/destroy
- Accessible only to authenticated users with operator role (new role concept)

## Out of scope

- Replacing the admin HTTP endpoint — destructive operations (peer removal, GC trigger, config reload) stay on port 9090
- Write operations via JMAP for peers, retention policy, or signing key — these are imperative operations that do not map cleanly to JMAP object lifecycle
- Building a custom JMAP client — the whole point is that existing clients work

## Acceptance criteria
- Creating a Mailbox named 'comp.lang.rust' in a JMAP client causes the server to subscribe to that group and begin accepting articles
- Destroying that Mailbox unsubscribes (with a grace period / confirmation flag to avoid accidental data loss)
- GET /jmap/session advertises urn:ietf:params:jmap:usenet-ipfs-admin for operator-role users
- Peer/get returns the same data as GET /admin/peers
- ServerStatus/get returns the same data as GET /admin/stats
- A standard JMAP client that does not know the custom capability ignores it gracefully
